title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
quote: In practice, we find that the block size 16 is large enough to efficiently utilize the GPU and small enough to avoid significant internal fragmentation in most workloads. Accordingly, vLLM sets its default block size as 16.
proves: Changes KV storage to fixed-size non-contiguous blocks. Block size 16 chosen from a sweep on 2 traces only (ShareGPT: 16-128 best; Alpaca: 16-32 best, larger degrades). Paged kernel costs 20-26% higher attention kernel latency vs FasterTransformer.
does_not_prove: Block size studied only on A100-class GPUs, OPT/LLaMA fp16, 2 traces, with 2023 kernels; never revisited for prefix-cache hit rate, unified memory, or quantized KV. No limitations section in abstract.
bearing: supports: block-size tradeoff gap on unified-memory/4-bit setups; threatens: naive block-size sweep on GPU (already done once)

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention (eviction and recovery)
quote: we implement an all-or-nothing eviction policy, i.e., either evict all or none of the blocks of a sequence.
proves: Preemption is fixed by design: all-or-nothing per sequence, FCFS scheduling. Swap vs recompute studied vs block size: swap bad at small blocks (PCIe small transfers), recompute overhead never above 20% of swap latency; comparable at 16-64.
does_not_prove: Partial (per-block) eviction and non-FCFS victim choice not studied. Swap/recompute tradeoff measured over PCIe only; on unified memory there is no PCIe copy, so the tradeoff is unmeasured there.
bearing: supports: partial-sequence preemption, swap-vs-recompute on unified memory; threatens: none directly

title: Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving
quote: LRUCache performs best under this dataset's patterns, likely due to the temporal proximity in request utilization.
proves: Changes where KV lives: disaggregated prefill/decode with a distributed KV pool. Hash block size 512 tokens. Eviction compared on Kimi trace: LRU 0.46 vs LFU 0.40 vs LengthAware 0.40 hit rate at 10k blocks; all converge to 0.55 at infinite capacity. Request-level output-length prediction left to future work.
does_not_prove: Eviction comparison is hit rate only (not TTFT or recompute cost), one trace, 3 simple policies; 512-token hash block not studied; evaluated with a dummy LLaMA2-70B.
bearing: threatens: simple LFU/length-aware eviction beating LRU on chat traces; supports: cost-aware eviction gap, prefix-block granularity gap

title: Mooncake: Trading More Storage for Less Computation - A KVCache-centric Architecture for Serving LLM Chatbot
quote: Mooncake is the serving platform for Kimi, an LLM chatbot service developed by Moonshot AI.
proves: Confirms Mooncake appeared at USENIX FAST 25 as a production system for Kimi.
does_not_prove: Venue page only; technical details taken from arXiv row A3.
bearing: context: venue confirmation for A3

title: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving
quote: the downtime of migration is nearly constant with increasing sequence lengths (roughly 20-30 ms)
proves: Changes KV movement: live migration of a request's KV across instances using multi-stage copy that relies on KV being append-only. Load metric freeness F=(M-sum V)/B with virtual usage. High-priority headroom 1,600 tokens chosen empirically without sweep; migration thresholds unstated.
does_not_prove: Migration thresholds and headroom never swept; evaluated on vLLM with LLaMA max 2k sequence; single-model-type. Future work: interplay of global scheduling with local scheduling.
bearing: supports: intra-instance analogs (e.g. headroom reservation, virtual-usage admission) on single device; threatens: cross-instance migration ideas (not doable on one laptop anyway)

title: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving (venue page)
quote: live migration mechanism for requests and their in-memory states
proves: Confirms OSDI 24 publication and the live-migration framing.
does_not_prove: Venue page only.
bearing: context: venue confirmation for A5

title: RetrievalAttention: Accelerating Long-Context LLM Inference via Vector Retrieval
quote: The size of the static pattern is consistently 640 (128 initial tokens + 512 tokens in the local window)
proves: Changes KV placement and access: ANN index over KV vectors in CPU memory, attention-aware search for OOD queries; accesses 1-3% of data; 128K context on RTX 4090 at 0.188 s/token. Static GPU pattern fixed at 640 tokens and top-k 100 without ablation.
does_not_prove: Single-batch only; assumes prefill done in advance; index build time not analyzed; static window size and top-k not swept; one index per query head (GQA cost).
bearing: supports: static-window size / top-k sensitivity gap, index-build cost gap; threatens: generic retrieval-based sparse attention novelty

title: FlexiCache: Leveraging Temporal Stability of Attention Heads for Efficient KV Cache Management
quote: We classify the least stable 25% of heads as unstable and the remaining heads as stable.
proves: FlexiCache is a vLLM-based per-head KV offload system: unstable heads keep all pages on GPU, stable heads keep top-K pages (64 pages of 16 tokens) and offload the rest to host; rerank every 16 steps. Up to 70% GPU memory reduction, 1.38-1.55x offline throughput.
does_not_prove: 25% split, page size 16 and rerank interval 16 are fixed without sweep; only token budget (1024/2048) varied. Assumes two-level GPU-CPU hierarchy; multi-node transfer open.
bearing: supports: rerank-interval and stable-head-fraction sensitivity gap; threatens: per-head offload as a new idea

title: FlexiCache (MLSys proceedings page)
quote: reduces GPU memory footprint for long-context requests by up to 70%
proves: Confirms FlexiCache is in Proceedings of Machine Learning and Systems 8 (MLSys 2026).
does_not_prove: Venue page only.
bearing: context: venue confirmation for A8

title: Strata: Hierarchical Context Caching for Long Context Language Model Serving
quote: a default threshold of 100 active token matches proved effective
proves: Strata is an SGLang-based GPU/CPU/SSD hierarchical KV cache: GPU-assisted I/O decouples GPU and host layouts (up to 4x lower disk-load latency), delay-hit deferral, balanced batching, bubble filling. Up to 5x lower TTFT vs vLLM+LMCache. Page size 1, delay-hit threshold 100, loading-bound ratio 100 all fixed without sweep.
does_not_prove: No eviction policy named or studied; thresholds not swept; single-instance only; disk tier unused in many benchmarks.
bearing: supports: delay-hit threshold sensitivity, eviction policy in tiered cache gap; threatens: layout-decoupling and loading-aware scheduling as new ideas

title: Strata (OSDI 26 page)
quote: We present Strata, a hierarchical context caching framework for long-context LLM serving.
proves: Confirms Strata at 20th USENIX OSDI 26.
does_not_prove: Venue page only.
bearing: context: venue confirmation for A10

title: vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention
quote: We find that the choice of page size does not affect vAttention as long as fragmentation is not a concern.
proves: Changes KV allocation: contiguous virtual KV with demand-mapped physical pages via CUDA VMM. Paged prefill kernels up to 37%/42% slower; block-table prep was 30% of decode latency in vLLM; up to 1.23x throughput. Page size studied (64KB-2MB).
does_not_prove: CUDA-specific; decode throughput only matches PagedAttention; swap to CPU left as future work. Not tested on unified memory where VMM semantics differ.
bearing: threatens: claims that paging cost dominates; supports: measuring block-table/paging overhead on Metal

title: vLLM design doc: prefix_caching (title not recorded)
quote: We only cache full blocks.
proves: vLLM prefix cache: LRU free-queue eviction; blocks of a finished request are freed in reverse so the last block is evicted first, because it hashes more tokens and is less likely reused; only full blocks are hashed.
does_not_prove: No measurement of hit rate or cost; partial-block caching and cost-aware eviction not evaluated.
bearing: supports: partial-block prefix caching gap, cost-aware eviction in vLLM; threatens: nothing

title: LMSYS blog post on SGLang, 2024-01-17 (title not recorded)
quote: We implement a Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policy, complemented by a cache-aware scheduling policy
proves: RadixAttention keeps prompt and generation KV in a radix tree, LRU leaf eviction, cache-aware (longest-prefix-first) scheduling.
does_not_prove: LRU chosen by default, no policy comparison in blog.
bearing: threatens: radix/prefix sharing as new idea; supports: eviction-policy gap on radix trees

title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
quote: novel optimizations like RadixAttention for KV cache reuse
proves: SGLang paper reports up to 6.4x throughput with RadixAttention among other optimizations.
does_not_prove: Abstract page only; venue (NeurIPS 2024) not shown on page.
bearing: context for A14

title: HiCache design (SGLang docs)
quote: Uses hit-count tracking to back up only frequently accessed data
proves: HiCache extends radix tree across GPU/host/storage tiers with selectable write policies (write_through, write_through_selective, write_back), prefetch policies, prefetch threshold 256 tokens, layouts layer_first (GPU default) / page_first.
does_not_prove: Docs give no data on which write policy or layout wins under which workload.
bearing: supports: tier write-policy comparison study (exposed knob, unstudied); threatens: building tiered cache from scratch

title: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
quote: 10 % of KV$ blocks contribute to 77 % of the reuses.
proves: Alibaba trace study: single-turn requests are 97% of hits in to-B trace; 80% of reuse within 10 min (Trace A) or 10 s (Trace B); workload-aware eviction beats LRU/FIFO/LFU/S3-FIFO by 8.1-23.9% hit rate but only 1.5-3.9% over the best baseline; up to 41.4% mean response time gain vs LRU.
does_not_prove: Single-instance eviction only; on Trace B policy falls back to LRU; reasoning workloads not covered.
bearing: threatens: eviction-policy tweaks (small gain over best baseline); supports: reasoning/agent workload KV reuse gap

title: Jenga: Effective Memory Management for Serving LLM with Heterogeneity
quote: employs a two-level memory allocator, leveraging the least common multiple (LCM) of embedding sizes
proves: Changes KV allocation for heterogeneous layers (sliding window, Mamba, cross-attention, spec decode): up to 79.6% better memory utilization, up to 4.92x throughput on vLLM.
does_not_prove: SOSP venue not confirmed on opened page. Targets heterogeneous models; not studied on Apple silicon.
bearing: threatens: hybrid-model KV allocator ideas; supports: per-layer-type eviction policy study

title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
quote: typically evict KV caches using a Least Recently Used (LRU) policy, which fails to anticipate future agent usage and often discards KV caches shortly before their reuse.
proves: Replaces LRU with steps-to-execution eviction from an Agent Step Graph plus CPU-to-GPU prefetch; up to 1.83x (single workflow) and 2.19x (many workflows) vs SGLang hierarchical radix cache.
does_not_prove: Needs workflow graph known in advance; not general chat.
bearing: threatens: future-aware eviction for agents; supports: eviction without workflow hints gap

title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
quote: selectively recomputes the KV values of a small subset of tokens
proves: Changes KV reuse to non-prefix chunks with selective recompute; TTFT 2.2-3.3x lower and throughput 2.8-5x higher vs full recompute.
does_not_prove: Venue not shown on page; recompute fraction knob and quality limits not covered by abstract.
bearing: threatens: non-prefix KV reuse as new idea; supports: recompute-fraction sensitivity study

title: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference
quote: extracts and stores KV caches generated by modern LLM engines (vLLM and SGLang) out of the GPU memory
proves: KV offload/sharing layer across engines and queries; up to 15x throughput on multi-round QA and document analysis. Default chunk size 256 (per A10).
does_not_prove: Chunk size choice not studied in opened text.
bearing: threatens: KV offload layer as new idea; supports: chunk-size granularity gap

title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
quote: can be speculated by performing a minimal rehearsal
proves: Prefetches only important KV from host using a rehearsal with partial next-layer query weights and key cache; up to 3.00x over prior offloading systems.
does_not_prove: Offloading over PCIe; unified memory removes the transfer that InfiniGen hides.
bearing: threatens: speculative KV prefetch novelty; supports: re-evaluating offload ideas on unified memory

title: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
quote: DistServe assigns prefill and decoding computation to different GPUs, hence eliminating prefill-decoding interferences.
proves: Prefill/decode disaggregation placed by cluster bandwidth; 7.4x more requests or 12.6x tighter SLO.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not discuss KV transfer cost; multi-GPU only.
bearing: low relevance on one laptop; context for KV transfer line

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
quote: novel admission and eviction policies that more judiciously assess potential cache entries
proves: Prefix cache for hybrid attention+SSM models with admission and FLOP-efficiency-aware eviction; up to 34.4x higher token hit rate, 617 ms lower TTFT.
does_not_prove: Hybrid models only; the FLOP-per-byte eviction idea not tested on pure-attention models.
bearing: threatens: cost-aware (FLOP-saved per byte) eviction novelty; supports: porting that score to pure transformers

title: kvcached
quote: it enables elastic and demand-driven KV cache allocation, improving GPU utilization under dynamic workloads.
proves: Virtual-memory elastic KV allocation library integrated with SGLang and vLLM (tested up to vLLM v0.30.0), for GPUs shared between workloads.
does_not_prove: No paper numbers opened; CUDA-only.
bearing: threatens: elastic KV pool idea on GPU; supports: elastic KV sizing on unified memory (shared with OS)

title: RetroInfer: A Vector Storage Engine for Scalable Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: a vector storage engine that realizes a sparsity-based KV cache for long-context inference
proves: RetrievalAttention successor: clustered wave index with GPU centroids plus wave buffer; up to 4.4x decode throughput vs full attention at 120K, 12.2x over sparse baselines at 1M tokens.
does_not_prove: Numbers changed across versions; targets GPU+CPU split.
bearing: threatens: retrieval/cluster-based KV index novelty

title: ShadowKV: KV Cache in Shadows for High-Throughput Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: stores the low-rank key cache and offloads the value cache
proves: Low-rank keys on GPU, values offloaded, sparse KV reconstructed on the fly; up to 6x batch, 3.04x throughput on A100.
does_not_prove: Venue not shown; offload benefit depends on discrete GPU memory.
bearing: threatens: low-rank key + offload novelty

title: KunServe: Parameter-centric Memory Management for Efficient Memory Overloading Handling in LLM Serving
quote: Prior KVCache-centric approaches handle overloading by dropping, migrating, or swapping KVCache.
proves: Llumnix follow-up: under overload, drop replicated parameters instead of KV; up to 72.2x lower tail TTFT vs Llumnix, vLLM, InferCept.
does_not_prove: Needs multiple GPUs with parameter replicas.
bearing: threatens: KV-only overload handling as complete; low direct relevance to one device
